properties.name: People are modellable inside the design, not only around it — organisation, role, and who performs a function
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-07, from the UAF audit: the Personnel domain has NO vocabulary in reflow2. Two people-shaped types exist and neither is this — `Contributor` is who authored the design, `Actor` is who the designed system serves. Both sit outside the system being designed.

WHAT CANNOT BE SAID TODAY: which role performs a function; the organisation a function belongs to; a post, a competence, or a responsibility assignment; who is accountable for a component. So an organisational view, a manning view, or a responsibility matrix has nothing to project from — and "which function is allocated to which system" (already answered by ALLOCATED_TO) has no counterpart for "which function is allocated to which PERSON or ROLE".

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND reflow2, which is the reason this is a requirement and not a curiosity: reflow2 itself is a tool with an agent and one user, so people barely appear inside its design and their absence is invisible here. Almost every non-software project has people IN the design — a beamline has operators, a satellite programme has crews and controllers, a hospital system has clinicians. `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` says fixes are judged by what they do for somebody else's project, and this is a gap only somebody else's project would feel.

NOT SPECIFIED HERE, deliberately: whether this is one node type or several, whether a role is a first-class node or a property on an edge, and whether reflow2 should follow UAF's Post/Role/Competence split or a simpler shape. Those are design questions and picking one now would foreclose them.
